s1.syndrome_frame: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae in a child
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex
Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on face, trunk, and extremities
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae in a child
salient_findings: Hyperkeratotic plaques with distinct borders and annular appearance
key_facts: Normal growth and development for age and sex
Multiple areas of erythema, vesicles, and bullae on face, trunk, and extremities
Skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation
Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation c.482T>C (p. L161P) in KRT1

differentials: Focal palmoplantar keratoderma with oral mucosal hyperkeratosis
per_call: Focal palmoplantar keratoderma with oral mucosal hyperkeratosis

shortlist.label: Epidermolytic hyperkeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation in KRT1, and skin-punch biopsy showed hyperkeratosis and bullae formation

shortlist.label: Bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of recurring skin eruptions with vesicles and bullae, and histopathology showing hyperkeratosis and vacuolization

shortlist.label: Ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical features and histopathological findings, including hyperkeratosis and bullae formation

shortlist.label: Keratinopathic ichthyosis
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic variation in KRT1 and clinical presentation of skin lesions with hyperkeratosis and bullae

shortlist.label: Pachyonychia congenita
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical features of palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and skin lesions with hyperkeratosis and bullae, although less likely due to absence of nail findings

raw.rationale: The patient's skin-punch biopsy revealed hyperkeratosis, distinct vacuolization in the granular and upper spinous layers, and bullae formation within the epidermis, which are characteristic features of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. Additionally, the genetic testing revealed a heterozygous variation in KRT1, a gene commonly associated with epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

rejected.label: Bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma
rejected.why: Although similar, the specific genetic variation and biopsy findings point more directly to epidermolytic hyperkeratosis

rejected.label: Ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and genetic findings do not specifically align with ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens

rejected.label: Keratinopathic ichthyosis
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, but the specific findings suggest a more precise diagnosis of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis

rejected.label: Pachyonychia congenita
rejected.why: The clinical features and genetic findings do not align with pachyonychia congenita, which typically involves nail and palmoplantar keratoderma
